name: Korea Masters
stakes: This week offers a crucial opportunity for India's top shuttlers to gain valuable ranking points and build confidence on the international circuit, especially for those aiming for a strong second half of the season.
summary: India's campaign at the Korea Masters, a Super 300 event, sees a strong but largely untested contingent as the main draw gets underway. Top-ranked men's doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, currently World No. 5, will be looking to assert their dominance, while former World Champion PV Sindhu, ranked 9th, seeks a deep run to build momentum after some recent struggles. Both enter their opening rounds with opponents yet to be determined.In men's singles, Lakshya Sen (World No. 14) and veteran HS Prannoy (World No. 24) are also in the fray, aiming to make their mark. The women's doubles pair of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, ranked 16th, and rising singles talent Malvika Bansod (World No. 31) round out the key Indian entries. While the draws for these prominent names are still taking shape, India has already seen some early success, with Tanvi Sharma advancing to an all-Indian clash against Shriyanshi Valishetty in the women's singles second round, and the men's doubles pair of Garaga and Roy also progressing.
